profile.reading:
Atman Data Center Warsaw-1 sits at ul. Grochowska 21A in the Praga-Poludnie district of Warsaw and is the oldest and largest of the Polish operator Atman's data centre sites. Atman publishes the campus specification in unusual detail, and it is worth separating the four different power numbers it gives, because they measure different things.

The campus has an energy capacity allocation of 57 MW, delivered over autonomous medium voltage lines. That is the utility allocation to the site and not an IT load. Behind it sit 26 transformers of 42,720 kVA total, static UPS plant rated at 29,460 kVA, and 16 diesel generators totalling 23,800 kVA, which are standby generation rather than continuous on-site generation. The only stated IT load figure is for a single building, F6, commissioned in 2021, which Atman describes as 1,440 square metres of technical space with a guaranteed 3.6 MW of IT power. Rack level provision is up to 10 kW per rack, with four 16 A 230 V feeds per rack, two from the A supply and two from the B supply.

Physically the campus runs to 8 data centre buildings with 12,428 square metres of gross data centre area, and Atman says it has room for 5 more server buildings adding roughly 7,000 square metres of server area. Raised floor loading is rated to 1,500 kilograms per square metre over a floor void of 500 to 700 millimetres, with 47U racks. Cooling uses computer room air conditioning units in N plus one redundancy, held at 18 to 27 degrees Celsius and 30 to 70 percent relative humidity. Fibre enters through diverse redundant duct routes and Atman operates a carrier neutral policy. The site holds the DCOS-4 certificate, the top level of the Data Centre Operations Standard issued by EPI, and Atman states the campus runs on 100 percent renewable electricity. The facility is independently listed in PeeringDB as ATMAN Data Center Warsaw-1, with the code WAW-1 and the same Grochowska 21A address, alongside Atman sites in Katowice, elsewhere in Warsaw and at Duchnice.

Atman itself dates to 1993 as Poland's first commercial internet service provider. It launched the country's first inter-operator internet exchange in 1997, the ancestor of today's Atman-IX, began offering colocation in 2002, and started dedicated data centre operations in 2008. The exchange still runs from this Grochowska campus, which makes Warsaw-1 an interconnection point as much as a colocation estate.
profile.research_note: Rewritten 2026-09-05. Removed the datacentermap.com citation, a banned source for this registry, and replaced it with a live PeeringDB API lookup confirming facility 2570, ATMAN Data Center Warsaw-1 (WAW-1, Grochowska 21A), org Atman Sp. z o.o. Re-fetched the operator facility page and added detail the prior pass did not carry: 26 transformers at 42,720 kVA, floor void 500/700 mm, 47U racks, CRAC units at N plus one, 18 to 27 C and 30 to 70 percent humidity, and 4 x 16 A / 230 V per rack from A and B supplies. Power discipline was the main fix here: the prior page stored 57 MW in it_capacity_mw and implied it was IT capacity. The operator calls it an energy capacity allocation, so the reading now separates utility allocation (57 MW), UPS plant (29,460 kVA), standby diesel generation (16 units, 23,800 kVA) and the only stated IT load (3.6 MW guaranteed in building F6). The it_capacity_mw column value of 57 is wrong on that basis and should be corrected in a separate numeric pass, which is out of scope for this content pass.
